Show the code observers, crash catalog, engine checks, five stress runners, report builder
  1. PerformanceObserver, ReportingObserver and __gfx wrapper. Scoped LoAF, long-task, CLS, event-timing, ReportingObserver and /api/reports filing.
  2. Crash and loss catalog. Links each historical bug to its standalone repro and localStorage key.
  3. Eight engine regression checks. Isolated fixtures that retire their canvas after each check.
  4. 2D DOM wall stress test. Up to 128 live interactive elements per frame with optional rotation and reflow churn.
  5. Snapshot ring-buffer stress test. Continuous captureElementImage() and close().
  6. WebGL 2 multi-texture + mipmap + FBO stress test. 16 live mutating DOM textures and a chromatic wave post-pass.
  7. WebGPU upload stress test. Eight live elements via drawElementImageToTexture() on the shared device.
  8. DOM, iframe and geometry churn test. Animated iframe child, live button hit-testing and transient drawable nodes.
  9. Markdown report builder. Formats browser details, observer telemetry, repro results, engine checks and stress stats.

How it works

  • Pressing "Run full Canary suite (automated)" opens /crashes/suite/runner.html immediately inside the click handler with noopener (so the popup blocker doesn't block it and the runner sits in a separate renderer process). Once Phase 1 completes or detects a renderer crash via the runner heartbeat, Phases 2 and 3 continue automatically right on this page.
  • observers.js attaches PerformanceObserver for long-animation-frame, longtask, layout-shift and event, plus ReportingObserver for crash, intervention and deprecation. Every timed stress benchmark runs inside a scoped observer window.
  • Detected runner crashes are filed to /api/reports via window.__gfx.report('canary-crash', …) and the end-of-run summary is filed via window.__gfx.report('canary-suite', …) (outside localhost, matching the site's guard).

Findings

Measured on 2026-11-24 on macOS (Apple M4 Pro, ANGLE Metal) comparing Chrome 158.0.8127.88 and Chrome Canary 160.0.8180.0 with CanvasDrawElement and ScopedViewTransitions enabled.

  • Four renderer crashes that died in Chrome 158 are fixed in Canary 160.0.8180.0: removing an iframe inside a paint handler (iframe-in-paint.html button B), calling adoptNode() on a painted drawable canvas into a same-origin iframe (adopt-painted-canvas.html button A), and both modes of the 4-canvas WebGL loseContext() stress repro (lose-context-stress.html buttons A and B) all crashed Chrome 158 and all survive with no crash in Canary 160.
  • Three earlier Chromium 157 failures were already fixed by Chrome 158 (and stay fixed in Canary 160): opacity: 0.02 around a drawable canvas inside a drawn iframe (opacity-in-drawn-iframe.html), same-task moveBefore() out and back into a drawable canvas, and clearElementGeometry() clearing the hit box.
  • One renderer crash still reproduces in Canary 160.0.8180.0: calling element.startViewTransition() on a drawable child of a drawable canvas (view-transition-drawable-child.html button A) still crashes the renderer in both Chrome 158 and Canary 160.
  • Four non-crashing engine bugs still reproduce in Canary 160.0.8180.0: stale hit-test cache after moving a drawn element without toggling an attribute; 9-argument source-rect draw leaving the hit region clipped after updateElementGeometry(); a nested plain <canvas> inside a padded drawable element drawing shifted by minus its padding; and continuous ctx.rotate() with drawElementImage() dropping lines of text on Apple Metal (2 of 60 frames lost over 15% of dark text pixels; fixed angle lost 0).
  • All six heavy stress workloads hold 60 fps in Canary 160 on Apple M4 Pro Metal with 0 context losses and 0 errors: 128 live 2D DOM cards with reflow churn (0.38 ms avg paint), 24-deep captureElementImage() trail (0.02 ms/capture), 16 live mutating WebGL 2 textures + mipmaps + FBO + periodic backing-store resize (0.23 ms upload), 8 live WebGPU drawElementImageToTexture() uploads (0.20 ms upload), and live DOM + iframe + hit-test churn.
  • Not verified on Android Canary: the three Android Chrome 159 losses (willReadFrequently on a drawable canvas, repeated getImageData(), and float16 readback) and the solid-white transparent WebGL bug did not reproduce on desktop macOS and need a run on an Android phone with Canary.
